– the failing test (signature + snippet),

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
The failure and bug report point to a problem in the method DateUtils.isSameLocalTime(Calendar cal1, Calendar cal2). The test case compares two Calendar instances with the same hour and minute values but different time zones or offsets. The bug report notes that the method incorrectly returns true when it compares the HOUR field of the Calendar, which returns the hour in 12-hour format (0-11), and not the 24-hour format which would distinguish between morning and afternoon.

Looking at the code of isSameLocalTime method, it compares several fields of the calendars using Calendar.get(field):

- MILLISECOND
- SECOND
- MINUTE
- HOUR
- DAY_OF_YEAR
- YEAR
- ERA
- class of the calendar objects

The critical problem is here:

```java
cal1.get(Calendar.HOUR) == cal2.get(Calendar.HOUR)
```

Calendar.HOUR is the 12-hour clock hour (0-11). This means that 13:00 and 1:00 would be considered the same hour, causing incorrect equality results when the time is in the afternoon.

The correct field to compare to account for the full 24-hour day is Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY (0-23). If both calendars have 13:45, their HOUR field (12-hour) would be 1, but their HOUR_OF_DAY would be 13. By using HOUR, the method fails in matching the true local time.

The test case uses two Calendar instances set to 13:45 hours, which is afternoon, so this bug causes the method to return true even if the underlying milliseconds differ due to timezone differences.

The bug report explicitly illustrates this issue with example milliseconds and the comment about comparing cal1.get(Calendar.HOUR) == cal2.get(Calendar.HOUR) as incorrect.

No other fields seem problematic. The DAY_OF_YEAR, YEAR, and ERA checks ensure the same date. The MILLISECOND, SECOND, and MINUTE checks verify finer time details.

Therefore, changing

```java
cal1.get(Calendar.HOUR) == cal2.get(Calendar.HOUR)
```

to 

```java
cal1.get(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY) == cal2.get(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY)
```

will fix the problem and make the method behave correctly for local time comparisons.

Recent bug reports retrieved are irrelevant to this issue.

# Diagnosis

The bug in DateUtils.isSameLocalTime occurs because the method compares Calendar.HOUR (12-hour clock) instead of Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY (24-hour clock). This causes the method to treat times like 1 PM and 1 AM as the same hour, resulting in incorrect true returns when comparing local times. The failing test and bug report confirm this. Changing the comparison in the method from HOUR to HOUR_OF_DAY will fix the issue.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
